introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper. Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D. Mobile phones are NOT allowed in the examination room.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.
incertitudes: Scan photocopié avec filigrane (gcerevision.com, ignoré) : accents, élisions et apostrophes relus sur un rendu à 200 dpi, aucune zone illisible. Les blancs imprimés sont écrits « ____ ». Q23 : le sujet imprime « qu’i. » (le « l » est illisible, lu « qu’il »).
Q1 passée en question ouverte : B (La camarade qui est entrée est très gentille) et D (Une camarade qui est entrée est très gentille) sont toutes deux grammaticales ; aucune lettre désignée.

Q20 passée en question ouverte : B (n’est pas bon de se précipiter) et C (faut vite faire ce qu’on a à faire) sont toutes deux défendables pour le proverbe « Rien ne sert de courir. Il faut partir à point » ; aucune lettre désignée.

Clés défendables par deux options, qcm conservés : Q28 (a du / b le, « le sable » possible avec un contexte), Q7 (c à vélo / a en vélo, familier), Q50 (a double championne olympique / c connue dans le monde entier), Q49 (d convaincre / c finally succeeded, vague), Q46 (c two-time departmental champion / d twice very successful), Q27 (c lesquels, registre soutenu ; la forme usuelle serait « qui », absente des options).

Q13 : l’option B est imprimée « Accueillant » avec une majuscule ; recopié tel quel. Q40 : l’option A est imprimée « Ne t’es lavé-tu pas? » (ordre fautif) ; recopiée telle quelle. Q15, Q43 et Q44 sont des questions de traduction glissées parmi les questions de grammaire ; thème « translation into French ».

questions.enonce_markdown:
____ camarade qui est entrée est très gentille.

*Options as printed:* A) Un B) La C) Le D) Une
questions.corrige_markdown: "Camarade" is feminine here ("entrée" is feminine), so "Un" and "Le" are impossible. Two feminine options remain: "La camarade qui est entrée est très gentille" (definite, natural because the relative clause identifies a particular girl) and "Une camarade qui est entrée est très gentille" (indefinite, grammatical but less natural as a statement about one identified person). Because both B and D are defensible, no letter is designated; the Board most probably expects B. Rule: a noun takes the article of its gender, and a definite article is used when the noun is identified by a relative clause.
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: La tante de Nadine est la ____ de cette école.
questions.corrige_markdown: "La" shows a feminine head of the school: "la directrice" (the headmistress). "Direction" is a noun meaning management, not a person, "dirigeante" (leader) is rarely used for a school and "directeur" is masculine. Rule: the feminine of "directeur" is "directrice". **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Il y a de ____ meubles dans ce salon.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Meubles" is masculine plural, so the adjective must be masculine plural: "beaux" (plural of "beau"). "Jolies" is feminine plural, and "joli" and "beau" are singular. "De" replaces "des" before a plural adjective placed before the noun ("de beaux meubles"). Rule: the adjective agrees in gender and number with its noun. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Qui va ____ va sûrement!
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence is the proverb "Qui va lentement va sûrement" (slow and steady wins the race). "Gentiment", "régulièrement" and "subitement" do not complete the proverb. Rule: a proverb is recalled as a whole. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Jean écrit une lettre à sa mère. Il ____ écrit une lettre.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Écrire une lettre à quelqu'un" takes an indirect object (à sa mère), replaced by the indirect pronoun "lui": "Il lui écrit une lettre". "La", "l'" and "l'a" are direct-object forms (and "l'a" would add an auxiliary). Rule: "à + person" is replaced by lui (singular) or leur (plural). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Marie aime ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: After the verb "aimer", a second verb stays in the infinitive: "aime danser". "Dansé" and "dansée" are past participles and "danse" is a conjugated form. Rule: verb + verb = the second verb is an infinitive. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon frère va à l’école ____ vélo.
questions.corrige_markdown: The standard preposition with a two-wheeled vehicle ridden astride is "à": "aller à vélo". "Sur" and "par" are not used in this expression. "En vélo" is heard in everyday speech but "à vélo" is the standard form expected at this level. Rule: à vélo, à moto, but en voiture, en bus. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Moussa est intelligent ____ très désordonné.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence opposes two qualities (intelligent / very untidy), so the conjunction of opposition "mais" is needed. "Car" gives a cause, "or" introduces a premise in an argument and "donc" a consequence. Rule: mais = but, it expresses contrast. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ école est située à l’entrée de la ville.
questions.corrige_markdown: "École" is feminine but starts with a vowel, so the masculine form of the possessive is used for the sound: "son école". "Sa" cannot stand before a vowel, "leurs" is plural and "ta" is the second person. Rule: before a feminine noun starting with a vowel, ma/ta/sa become mon/ton/son. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Ma mère ne mange pas ____ biscuits.
questions.corrige_markdown: After a negation of quantity ("ne ... pas"), the indefinite or partitive article becomes "de": "ne mange pas de biscuits". "Des" and "du" are not kept in the negative, and "les" would change the meaning (particular biscuits). Rule: in the negative, un/une/des/du/de la become de (d'). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Comment ____ ?
questions.corrige_markdown: The reflexive verb "s'appeler" in the second person singular is "tu t'appelles", and in an inverted question "t'appelles-tu" (the pronoun "te" stays before the verb, the verb takes -s). "T'appelle-tu" has the wrong ending, "appelles-tu" lacks the reflexive pronoun and "tu t'appelle" lacks the -s. Rule: in the second person singular of verbs in -er the ending is -es. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Nous sommes fiers de nos enfants. Ils sont aussi fiers ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Être fier de" requires "de", and the possessive pronoun replaces "leurs enfants": "fiers des leurs" (de + les leurs = des leurs). "Les leurs" lacks the preposition, "du leurs" mixes singular and plural and "des leur" lacks the plural -s. Rule: de + les = des; the possessive pronoun is le/la/les leur(s). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: L’aînée de la famille est très ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: "L'aînée" is feminine singular, and "très" requires an adjective: "accueillante" (welcoming). "Accueillie" is a past participle, "accueillant" (masculine, printed with a capital) does not agree and "accueillent" is a verb form. Rule: the adjective agrees with the subject. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Il est arrivé quand papa ____ déjà.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence describes a state in progress in the past when the other action happened ("il est arrivé"), so the imperfect "dormait" is used. "Dort" is the present, "dormit" is the literary simple past and "a dormi" presents a completed action. Rule: the imperfect describes the background situation, the passé composé the event. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Translate into French: “Any student is entitled to a scholarship”.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Any" in the sense of "every, whichever" is "n'importe quel": "N'importe quel élève a droit à la bourse". "Même quel" is not French, and "quelques" and "certains" mean "some", which changes the meaning. Rule: any = n'importe quel (+ noun). **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

choix.texte: Même quel élève a droit à la bourse.
N’importe quel élève a droit à la bourse.
Quelques élèves ont droit à la bourse.
Certains élèves ont droit à la bourse.

questions.enonce_markdown: -Buvez-vous <u>du vin</u> ? - Oui, nous ____ buvons.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Du vin" is a partitive (an unspecified quantity), replaced by the pronoun "en": "nous en buvons". "Le" and "la" replace a definite noun and "y" replaces a place or "à + thing". Rule: du/de la/des + noun = en. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Maman et sa camarade ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: With the auxiliary être in a reflexive verb, the past participle agrees with the subject when the reflexive pronoun is a direct object. The subject "Maman et sa camarade" is feminine plural: "se sont rencontrées". "Rencontrée" is singular, "rencontrés" is masculine and "rencontrer" is an infinitive. Rule: the participle of a reflexive verb agrees with the subject. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: « Thomas écrit la lettre » devient à la voix passive
questions.corrige_markdown: In the passive, the tense of the active verb is kept: "écrit" is present, so the passive is "est écrite" (present of être + participle). The other options use the passé composé, the future and the imperfect. Rule: active tense = tense of the auxiliary être in the passive. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

choix.texte: La lettre a été écrite par Thomas.
La lettre sera écrite par Thomas.
La lettre était écrite par Thomas.
La lettre est écrite par Thomas.

questions.enonce_markdown: Je te donne ce conseil ____ tu deviennes sage.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "deviennes" is in the subjunctive and the clause expresses the purpose of the advice, so "pour que" (so that) is needed. "Parce que" and "puisque" give a cause and take the indicative, "alors que" expresses opposition or time. Rule: pour que + subjunctive = purpose. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown:
« Rien ne sert de courir. Il faut partir à point » veut dire qu’il ____.

*Options as printed:* A) faut toujours se précipiter juste un peu B) n’est pas bon de se précipiter C) faut vite faire ce qu’on a à faire D) ne faut jamais courir
questions.corrige_markdown: The proverb means that there is no point in rushing at the last moment; one must start in time. Two options reflect part of this: B ("it is not good to rush") captures the first half, and C ("one must quickly do what one has to do") captures the second half, "partir à point" (start in good time). A is contradictory and D ("one must never run") is too absolute. Because B and C are both defensible, no letter is designated. Rule: a proverb is understood by its overall moral.

questions.enonce_markdown: Marie chante ____ que sa sœur.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Chante" is a verb, so the comparative of the adverb "bien" is needed: "mieux". "Plus mieux" is a double comparative, and "meilleur" and "meilleure" are adjectives. Rule: bien (adverb) gives mieux; bon (adjective) gives meilleur. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Justine a oublié ____ faire son devoir.
questions.corrige_markdown: The verb "oublier" is followed by "de" before an infinitive: "oublier de faire". "À", "pour" and "par" are not used. Rule: oublier de + infinitive. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le surveillant général ne le punira pas à moins qu’i. ____ une faute.
questions.corrige_markdown: The conjunction "à moins que" is followed by the subjunctive: "à moins qu'il commette une faute" (unless he commits an offence). "A commis", "commet" and "commettra" are indicative forms. Rule: à moins que + subjunctive. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Christelle parle à ses parents. Elle ____ parle.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Parler à quelqu'un" takes an indirect object; for "ses parents" (plural) the pronoun is "leur" (invariable): "elle leur parle". "Leurs" is a possessive adjective, "les" is a direct pronoun and "à eux" is not placed before the verb. Rule: à + people = lui (singular) / leur (plural). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Cette année la famille ne mange pas à sa faim. Ceci veut dire que la famille ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Manger à sa faim" means to eat enough to satisfy one's hunger, so "ne pas manger à sa faim" means not to eat enough: "ne mange pas suffisamment". A would mean the family never eats when hungry, which is not the idiom, B has "ils" instead of "elle" and C is unrelated. Rule: manger à sa faim = eat enough. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: ne mange pas quand elle a faim
ne mange pas quand ils ont faim
ne mange pas ses repas favoris

questions.enonce_markdown: Le mois prochain, ____ seize ans.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Le mois prochain" indicates the future, and the subject is "je": the simple future of avoir is "j'aurai". "J'aurais" is the conditional, "j'aura" is the third person and "j'auras" the second person. Rule: future of avoir: j'aurai, tu auras, il aura. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: La police a entendu les suspects ____ ont tous nié les faits.
questions.corrige_markdown: The relative pronoun is the subject of "ont nié" and refers to "les suspects" (masculine plural): "lesquels" (a compound relative in formal style, the plain form being "qui", which is not offered). "Auxquels" is an indirect-object form, "les qui" is not French and "lesquelles" is feminine. Rule: the compound relative pronoun agrees in gender and number with its antecedent. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il a acheté ____ sable.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Sable" is a masculine noun denoting an unspecified quantity of a substance, so the partitive "du" is used: "il a acheté du sable". "Le" would mean a specific, known sand (possible only with a context), "de" is used after a negation or a quantity and "la" is feminine. Rule: partitive article for an unspecified amount: du (masculine), de la (feminine), de l' (vowel). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il faut que vous ____ la vérité.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Il faut que" is followed by the subjunctive. The subjunctive of "savoir" is "que je sache, que tu saches, qu'il sache, que nous sachions, que vous sachiez, qu'ils sachent". The correct form is therefore "sachiez". "Savez" is the present indicative, "saurez" the future, and "sachez" is the imperative. Rule: the subjunctive of savoir has the endings -ions and -iez for nous and vous. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Certaines femmes travaillent toujours ______.
questions.corrige_markdown: The gerund (en + present participle) expresses the manner of the action. The verb "se plaindre" keeps its reflexive pronoun: "en se plaignant" (while complaining). "En plaignant" changes the verb into "plaindre" (to pity), "se plaignant" lacks "en" and "en plaignante" is not a participle. Rule: gerund = en + participle in -ant, and the reflexive pronoun stays. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Papa, ____ moi!
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence identifies the speaker ("Papa, it's me!"), so "c'est" (ce + est) is needed. "Ces" and "ses" are determiners and "s'est" is a reflexive auxiliary form. Rule: c'est + pronoun is used to identify. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Trouvez le contraire du mot souligné. « Ses parents étaient <u>contents</u> de lui ».
questions.corrige_markdown: The opposite of "content" (pleased) is "mécontent" (displeased), formed with the prefix mé-. "Assez contents" and "peu contents" only reduce the degree, and "désagréables" (unpleasant) describes the person and not satisfaction with someone. Rule: the prefix mé- gives the opposite. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Les gens qui vivent en ville sont appelés des ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: People who live in a city are "citadins" (city dwellers). "Citoyens" are members of a state, "citadelles" are fortresses and "vilains" are ugly or (historically) peasants. Rule: citadin = who lives in a town; citoyen = who has civic rights. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Le Cameroun est un pays béni du nord ____ sud.
questions.corrige_markdown: The expression is "du nord au sud", where "au" is the contraction of "à + le" before the masculine noun "sud". "À le" is never written in full, "à" lacks the article and "aux" is plural. Rule: à + le = au. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Tout le monde ____ ce matin.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Tout le monde" (everybody) is grammatically third person singular, so the passé composé is "a travaillé". "Ont travaillé" makes the verb plural, "as travaillé" is second person and "a travailler" uses an infinitive instead of the participle. Rule: tout le monde takes a singular verb. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Il a vendu ____ auto bon marché.
questions.corrige_markdown: "Auto" is a feminine noun (une auto) beginning with a vowel. The demonstrative that agrees with a feminine noun is "cette": "cette auto". "Ce" and "cet" are masculine forms, and "sa" cannot stand before a vowel (it would be "son auto"). Rule: cette + feminine noun, even before a vowel. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - gender and number

questions.enonce_markdown: Le professeur est arrivé à 11 heures 45 minutes, c’est- à-dire à ______.
questions.corrige_markdown: 11:45 is a quarter of an hour before noon: "midi moins le quart". "Midi et quart" and "midi et un quart" mean 12:15, and "midi avant le quart" is not a French way to tell the time. Rule: moins le quart = quarter to; et quart = quarter past. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - numbers and fractions

questions.enonce_markdown: Mon fils, ______ attentif quand le professeur parle.
questions.corrige_markdown: The sentence is an order given to one person addressed as "tu" ("Mon fils"): the imperative of "être" is "sois". "Soyez" is for vous, "soyons" for nous and "soit" is the third person subjunctive. Rule: imperative of être: sois, soyons, soyez. **Answer: B.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: Elle a eu beaucoup de <u>succès</u> cette année. Quel est le synonyme du mot souligné ?
questions.corrige_markdown: "Succès" means success, and its synonym is "réussite". "Soucis" and "problèmes" mean worries, and "prières" means prayers. Rule: succès = réussite. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Mettez la phrase suivante à la forme négative. « T’es-tu lavé? »
questions.corrige_markdown: In an inverted question in a compound tense, "ne" goes before the pronoun and the auxiliary, and "pas" after the inverted subject, before the participle: "Ne t'es-tu pas lavé ?". A has the wrong word order ("lavé-tu"), B is not a negation of the same question and D adds a tag question that does not make the sentence negative. Rule: ne + pronoun + auxiliary-subject + pas + participle. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: ____ temps après le repas, ils ont repris le travail!
questions.corrige_markdown: "Quelque temps" (some time, a while) is the invariable determiner used with a singular noun. "Quelques" requires a plural noun, and "quel que" and "quels que" are used before a subjunctive ("quel que soit..."). Rule: quelque + singular noun = a certain amount of; quelques + plural. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Les enfants, je les ai ____ à l’église.
questions.corrige_markdown: With the auxiliary avoir, the past participle agrees with the direct object when it is placed before the verb. Here "les" (the children, masculine plural) comes before, so "accompagnés". "Accompagnent" is a conjugated verb, "accompagner" an infinitive and "accompagné" does not agree. Rule: the participle agrees with a preceding direct object. **Answer: D.**
themes: O Level French - tenses and moods

questions.enonce_markdown: “I am eighteen.” could be translated into French as:
questions.corrige_markdown: In French, age is expressed with the verb "avoir" and the word "ans": "J'ai dix-huit ans". "Je suis" is the anglicism, and "J'ai dix-huit" omits "ans", which is required. Rule: avoir + number + ans. **Answer: C.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

questions.enonce_markdown: We do our housework during weekends!
questions.corrige_markdown: "Housework" is "le ménage" (faire le ménage), and "during weekends" is rendered by "les week-ends". "Manège" is a merry-go-round, "la ménagère" is a housewife (a person) and "les travaux" means works or construction. Rule: faire le ménage = to do the housework. **Answer: A.**
themes: O Level French - translation into French

choix.texte: Nous faisons le ménage les week-ends!
Nous faisons le manège les week-ends!
Nous faisons la ménagère les week-ends!
Nous faisons les travaux les week-ends!

questions.enonce_markdown: Notre joie est à son ____.
questions.corrige_markdown: The expression "être à son comble" means to be at its height: "Notre joie est à son comble". "Comblé" and "comblée" are participles (fulfilled), and "complétude" is a rare abstract noun not used in this expression. Rule: à son comble = at its peak. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
**Passage for questions 46 to 50**

Mgobang, pendant les deux dernières années de ses études primaires, était déjà championne départementale du triple saut dames. Ses parents, dans la peur que leur fille abandonne les études, pour le sport, ont essayé de décourager l’enfant qu’ils trouvaient d’ailleurs très jeune.

Arrivée au collège, elle a eu les mêmes exploits. Quand elle a expliqué l’idée de ses parents à son professeur de sports, ce dernier est allé rencontrer la famille. Ce n’était pas facile, mais il a finalement réussi à convaincre Papa Benfa et Ma Maggi…

Aujourd’hui, double championne olympique, Mgobang est une véritable vedette connue dans le monde entier.

What remarkable thing did Mgobang do in her last two years in primary school?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says that during her last two years of primary school she was already departmental champion in the women's triple jump. Option C matches (two years, departmental, triple jump). B says "divisional", which is not in the text, A only says she was interested and D is vague and does not name the title. Rule: choose the option that keeps the exact details of the passage. **Answer: C.**

choix.texte: She was very interested in triple jump.
She was two-time divisional champion in triple jump.
She was two-time departmental champion in triple jump.
She was twice very successful in triple jump.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Why did her parents try to discourage her?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text gives two reasons: they feared that their daughter would abandon her studies for sport, and they found her very young. Only D contains both. A (fail) and B (abandon writing exams) change the fear, and C gives only the second reason. Rule: the complete answer combines every reason given in the text. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: They were afraid she would fail in her studies.
They were afraid she will abandon writing her exams.
They thought that she was very young.
She was very young, and they feared that she would abandon her studies.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

What happened while she was in college?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says "Arrivée au collège, elle a eu les mêmes exploits": at college she achieved the same feats as before. A is the faithful paraphrase. B (became a star) happens later, C is meaningless and D (powers) is not the idea. Rule: paraphrase the sentence of the text. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: She became a star with the same prowess.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

How was her sports teacher helpful to her?
questions.corrige_markdown: The text says that the teacher went to meet the family and that, although it was not easy, "il a finalement réussi à convaincre" her parents. The help lies in the result: he convinced them (D). A and B only describe the attempt, and C is vague (succeeded at what?). Rule: the answer to "how was he helpful" is what he achieved. **Answer: D.**

choix.texte: He met her parents and talked to them.
Though it was not easy, he discussed with her parents.
He finally succeeded with her parents.
He succeeded in convincing her parents.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(Passage for questions 46 to 50 above)

Why is Mgobang so popular today?
questions.corrige_markdown: The last paragraph says that today she is a double Olympic champion and a real star known in the whole world. The reason for her popularity is her title: she is a two-time Olympic champion (A). C ("known the world over") only restates her popularity rather than giving a reason, and B and D are not stated in the text. Rule: a "why" question asks for the cause, not for a restatement of the result. **Answer: A.**

choix.texte: She is a two-time Olympic champion.
She concentrated fully on sports and succeeded.
She is known the world over.
She showed the entire world that sports is good.
